Wi-Fi coverage in real workspaces

Measured indoor beacon strength across 32 locations and fit a compact path-loss model that captured distance and wall attenuation with R² = 0.93.

Case study

Measure how a real building reshapes wireless coverage.

Wi-FiWiresharkRegressionPath loss

The experiment

A monitor-mode WLAN card captured roughly 300 beacon frames at each of 32 locations inside the Centre for Innovation building. Distance from the access point, intervening walls, and RSSI were recorded across workspaces and floors.

The model

The fitted log-distance model used a reference RSSI of −31.3 dBm, a path-loss exponent of 2.81, and a wall attenuation factor near −3.03 dB per wall. The resulting fit reached an R² of 0.93.

Result

Signal strength followed the expected logarithmic decay with distance, but obstacles materially shifted the readings. For the measured environment, keeping devices within roughly ten metres helped maintain stronger than −65 dBm coverage, with elevated access-point placement and line of sight offering clear benefits.
